catalog_quote: 軽声について楊氏は,{太谷城関話にも軽声はあるが,その範囲は「普通話」ほど大きくない。太谷の二音節語の第二音節には軽声はなく,軽声はいくつかの語末・文末にのみ現われる。例えば,桌子・我的・甚嚒などなどで,聴いたところ陰入調に極めて近い。}と述べているが,5) 黄氏の発音では,これらは皆陰入と全く同一である。6) ... 組み合わせによっては変調のパターンを2通り有する場合が存在するが,その場合には,第二音節が軽く発音されると考えられる方をBパターンと呼び,そうでない方をAパターンと呼ぶことにする。 [fn.6, pp.30-31] ただ,黄氏の発音において,次の如き平声+平声のミニマルペアは,文末の環境に限り,上段の意味の場合には2音節とも比較的高く且つ長く発音され,下段の意味の場合には2音節とも比較的低く,特に第2音節は短くやや下降気味に発音されるようである。(カッコ内は「普通話」の相当する拼音。) 編排 [pieN33 p'ai33] 〈動〉排列する,編成する (biānpái) 〈動〉根も葉もないことで人を中傷する (biānpai) 東西 ... 〈名〉東西 (dōngxī) 〈名〉物 (dōngxi)

new_statements.translation: On the neutral tone, Yang [1983] states: 'Taigu town speech also has neutral tone (qingsheng), but its range is not as large as in Putonghua. The second syllable of Taigu disyllabic words does not carry neutral tone; neutral tone appears only in a few word-final and sentence-final items, e.g. □子, 我的, 甚□, which to the ear are extremely close to the yin-ru tone.' In Ms Huang's [Higuchi's informant's] pronunciation, however, these are all completely identical to the yin-ru tone. … For some tone combinations two sandhi patterns exist; in that case I call the one in which the second syllable is considered to be pronounced lightly the B pattern, and the other the A pattern.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Jin is a lexical-tone language (Taigu: 5 tones incl. two checked/ru tones; Taiyuan likewise 5). No source found states a positional word-stress rule. What the accessible descriptions say about prominence is negative/marginal: unlike Beijing Mandarin, central Shanxi Jin (Taigu, Taiyuan, Qixian, Xiaoyi) has few or no destressed neutral-tone second syllables in ordinary disyllabic words — both syllables keep (sandhi) tones; weak/toneless syllables are confined to a handful of suffixes and particles (子, 的, 么), realised like the short yin-ru tone, plus a lexically restricted 'B' sandhi pattern with a lightly pronounced second syllable (i.e. where weakening occurs it is the FINAL syllable that is weak, trochaic). Yagi 2019 quantifies this: neutral-tone rate 1-4% in central Jin points vs c. 50% at the northern (Datong-area) and southern edges of Shanxi.
new_statements.exceptions: Neutral-tone (weak) syllables limited to suffix 子, particles 的/么/了-type items and reduplications (Higuchi 1990: 25; Yagi 2019: 122 for Taiyuan); Higuchi fn.6: Beijing-type stress minimal pairs (編排 'arrange' vs 編派 'slander') are distinguished in Taigu only sentence-finally, the 'neutral' member having both syllables lower and the second shorter and slightly falling. Yagi 2019: northern Shanxi Jin (e.g. Shanyin 52%) and peripheral points have Beijing-like frequent neutral tone, so the 'no neutral tone' statement holds for the central (Bingzhou/Taiyuan) cluster, not all of Jin.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern disyllabic lexical words in citation/elicitation (二字組連読変調) and word-/sentence-final enclitics; no phrase-level stress description. Taigu data from one speaker (b.1957) plus Yang 1983; Yagi's figures are computed from published wordlists (Hou & Wen 1993).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Taigu 太谷 (Jin, Bingzhou 并州片 cluster, c. 50 km south of Taiyuan; no separate Glottolog code — nearest Glottolog dialect node is Taiyuan [taiy1243] under jiny1235). Yagi 2019's corroborating figures cover 42 Shanxi points and show the 'neutral tone nearly absent' property holds for the central cluster (Taiyuan, Qixian, Xiaoyi, Taigu) but NOT for northern Shanxi Jin (Datong-Shanyin area, c. 50% neutral-tone items) — so any catalog entry should be labelled 'central (Bingzhou) Jin / Taiyuan-Taigu'. Glottolog's other dialect nodes are Pingyao [ping1247] and Huhehaote [huhe1234]; nothing dialect-specific on stress was found for those.

tone_statements.translation: Grouping by tone shape, the tones of the Xinghuacun dialect fall into roughly 5 types: pingsheng, shangsheng, qusheng, yin-ru, yang-ru. MC voiced-obstruent shang has merged into qusheng; MC sonorant and voiced-obstruent ping have merged into yin-ru. … so the Xinghuacun pingsheng value is recorded as 13 … shangsheng as 51 … qusheng as 15. … Table 3, citation-tone values: Xinghuacun 13 51 15 23 421; Dongxiang subcluster (Tian 2019) 33 513 35 33 513; Bingzhou cluster [Taiyuan] (Wang 2012) 11 53 45 2 54.
tone_statements.summary: Xinghuacun (Fenyang, Lüliang Jin): five citation tones from acoustic measurement, ping 13, shang 51, qu 15, yin-ru 23, yang-ru 421; Bingzhou (Taiyuan) values 11 53 45 2 54 relayed for comparison.

sources.note: Survey (81 lexical items x 42 Shanxi points from Hou & Wen 1993): rate of neutral-tone (unstressed, tonally neutralised) final syllables is lowest in central Shanxi Jin (Qixian 1%, Xiaoyi 1%, Taigu 21%) and highest at the N and S ends (Shanyin 52%, Yuncheng 52%); word-final tone sandhi shows the complementary distribution. Taiyuan has no systematic word-final sandhi in non-reduplicated words; sandhi/neutral tone only in reduplications, particles and suffixes like 子 (citing Shen Ming 1998:6, Hao Xiaoming 2004:76) (pp.120-122). sources.citation: Iwata Ray 岩田礼 2001. 中国語の声調とアクセント / Tone and accent across the Chinese dialects. 音声研究 (J. Phonetic Soc. Japan) 5(1): 18-27 (J-STAGE open).
sources.note: Pan-Sinitic typology: in most dialects two lexically specified word stress patterns coexist, right-stressed (#US#) and left-stressed (#SU#, whose weak syllable = 'neutral tone'); Jin (晋語, part of Shanxi) is mentioned only as one of the few Mandarin-area groups showing the 'right spreading' subtype of left-stressed neutral-tone words (p.24). No Jin-specific stress-placement rule.

sources.note: First-hand fieldwork on Taigu (Jin, Bingzhou cluster, 50 km S of Taiyuan). No positional word-stress rule. Quotes Yang Shuzu 1983 (Taigu fangyan zhi p.6): Taigu has neutral tone (軽声) but far less than Putonghua; second syllables of disyllabic words are NOT neutral-toned; neutral tone only on a few word-/sentence-final items (子, 我的, 甚么), sounding like the yin-ru tone; Higuchi confirms his speaker pronounces these identically to yin-ru. tone.translation: Grouping by tone shape, the tones of the Xinghuacun dialect fall into roughly 5 types: pingsheng, shangsheng, qusheng, yin-ru, yang-ru. MC voiced-obstruent shang has merged into qusheng; MC sonorant and voiced-obstruent ping have merged into yin-ru. … so the Xinghuacun pingsheng value is recorded as 13 … shangsheng as 51 … qusheng as 15. … Table 3, citation-tone values: Xinghuacun 13 51 15 23 421; Dongxiang subcluster (Tian 2019) 33 513 35 33 513; Bingzhou cluster [Taiyuan] (Wang 2012) 11 53 45 2 54.
